facts.headline: Gaudí made sure his tower could never out-build God
facts.body_html: Sagrada Família's central tower finally topped out in February 2026 at 172.5 meters — 144 years after construction began. Gaudí deliberately designed it to stay shorter than Montjuïc hill nearby, so his creation would never surpass God's.

facts.headline: The mosaic dragon guarding Park Güell is secretly plumbing
facts.body_html: Gaudí's famous trencadís salamander is built from shattered tile and glass shards — and doubles as the overflow spout for a giant cistern hidden right beneath the park's main terrace.

facts.headline: This house's skull-shaped balconies tell a dragon-slaying legend
facts.body_html: Casa Batlló is a three-story tribute to Catalonia's patron saint: the scaled roof is the dragon's back, the bone-like columns and skull balconies are its victims, and the rooftop cross is Saint George's sword plunged into its spine.

facts.headline: Those 'bullet holes' in this square are actually bomb scars
facts.body_html: For decades, Franco's regime claimed the pockmarked walls of Plaça de Sant Felip Neri came from firing-squad executions. They're really from a 1938 aerial bombing that killed 42 people, many of them children sheltering inside the church.

facts.headline: You can walk an actual Roman city under these streets
facts.body_html: Beneath the Gothic Quarter, Barcelona's history museum preserves real streets and workshops from Barcino, the Roman colony founded here 2,000 years ago — laundries and wine vats still sitting underground.

facts.headline: Barcelona's most famous beach didn't exist 35 years ago
facts.body_html: Barceloneta beach is entirely man-made — planners trucked in sand and rebuilt the whole coastline for the 1992 Olympics. Before that, this stretch was industrial shoreline, not sand.

facts.headline: One concert hall in Europe runs almost entirely on sunlight
facts.body_html: Palau de la Música Catalana is lit by an inverted stained-glass skylight shaped like the sun — the only concert hall in Europe that performs by daylight alone. It's stunning, and it quietly wrecks the room's acoustics.
